excerpts.source: send_now:H().optional().describe("@internal True when the request is a client's Send now on a message that is waiting, not its Stop: it asks that the waiting messages reach the model now, as the terminal's send-now key does. It is not a Stop: it makes no later turn start aborted, cancels nothing that is queued, and ends no background task, subscription or other thing outside the running turn that a Stop ends. What it does depends on what the CLI holds when it reads the request, and the response's send_now says which. Without message_uuid every waiting user message counts, which may be another than the one pressed. With no user message waiting at the CLI it does nothing: a message the running turn has already taken in, or was started for, is being answered. With one waiting that is not in the queue yet (received and still being admitted, or already taken for the next turn), that the running turn is taking in at that moment, or with no turn under way, it also does nothing: the message runs when its place comes. With a person's message in the queue behind a turn under way, the CLI chooses how that turn makes way: it moves what the turn waits on to the background so that the turn takes the message in (and, if that fails, stops the turn later as a priority 'now' message does, without a marker), or it aborts that turn at once as a plain interrupt does (running tools are ended, the interruption marker is written, the result is an error_during_execution); what was queued ahead of the message still runs before it. Either way a sender learns that the turn has ended from the turn's result, not from this response. The message must already be at the CLI, or the request finds nothing waiting: a sender that still holds it delivers it first, or sends it with priority 'now', or sends a plain interrupt instead. Only the boolean true counts, and with cancel_queued:true the request is a Stop. Advertised by interrupt_send_now_v1 on system/init; a CLI without it handles the request as a plain interrupt."),message_uuid:o().optional().describe("@internal Read only beside send_now:true: the uuid of the user message that Send now was pressed on, in the very form in which that message reached the CLI (a session service may deliver it in lower case): it is compared as an exact string, as cancel_async_message compares. With it only that message counts as waiting. If the running turn has already taken it in or was started for it, or the CLI does not know it or does not count it as a person's, the request does nothing and answers 'nothing_waiting', whatever else waits. Once the request acts, it acts as without the name: everything queued decides between the move to the background and the abort, and goes along with the named message. An empty string is read as no name, and so is a null, which this schema does not admit but an encoder may write; any other value that is no string names nothing."),for_
